CHAPTER 2.3 · LEARNING AREA 2 · NOVEMBER · DECEMBER

The sine function

A gondola on the Ferris wheel rises and falls, the water in the harbour comes and goes, the socket delivers 50 oscillations per second. Such periodic processes are described by the sine function. You learn radian measure, develop the sine curve on the unit circle and change it with the amplitude and the period.

8 LESSONS2 UNITSPERIODICRADIANS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • give angles in degrees and in radians and convert between them
  • explain the sine function on the unit circle: zeros, maximum and minimum points, period $2\pi$
  • describe the effect of $a$ and $b$ in $y = a \cdot \sin(b \cdot x)$
  • model periodic processes and organise the types of functions from this year

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Radians and the unit circle

The thread fits around the circle a little more than six times, exactly $2\pi \approx 6.28$ times. That is why angles are also measured as arc lengths on the unit circle (radius 1): the full angle is $2\pi$, the straight angle $\pi$. If you let a point run around this circle, its height is the sine of the angle. If you plot the height against the angle, you get the sine curve.

KEY POINT · RADIANS AND THE SINE FUNCTION

$360^\circ \;\widehat{=}\; 2\pi$, $\;180^\circ \;\widehat{=}\; \pi$, $\;90^\circ \;\widehat{=}\; \tfrac{\pi}{2}$. Converting: $x = \dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ} \cdot \alpha$.

The point on the unit circle at the angle $x$ has the coordinates $(\cos x, \sin x)$.

$y = \sin x$: defined for all numbers, values from $-1$ to $1$, period $2\pi$, zeros $0, \pi, 2\pi, \ldots$, maximum point at $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, minimum point at $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, point-symmetric about the origin.

Calculator trap: in radian mode (RAD), $\sin 30 \approx -0.988$. For degrees the calculator must be set to DEG.

Periodic: $\sin(x + 2\pi) = \sin x$ for all $x$.

INTERACTIVE · FROM THE UNIT CIRCLE TO THE SINE CURVE

Let the point run around the circle. Its height is recorded on the right as a sine curve.

EXAMPLE 1 · CONVERTING

Convert $60^\circ$ to radians and $\tfrac{3\pi}{4}$ to degrees.

$60^\circ = \tfrac{60}{180}\pi =$ $\tfrac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.05$. $\;\tfrac{3\pi}{4} = \tfrac34 \cdot 180^\circ =$ $135^\circ$.

EXAMPLE 2 · THE SAME HEIGHT

Why is $\sin 150^\circ = \sin 30^\circ$?

The points at $30^\circ$ and $150^\circ$ are mirror images in the y-axis, so they are at the same height: both 0.5.

EXERCISES

Convert to radians: $45^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $270^\circ$. And to degrees: $\tfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$, $1$.

$\tfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$. $\;30^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $\approx 57.3^\circ$.

Read off on the unit circle: $\sin 0$, $\sin \tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\sin \pi$, $\sin \tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $\sin 2\pi$.

$0$, $1$, $0$, $-1$, $0$

Give all $x$ between $0$ and $2\pi$ for which $\sin x = 0.5$.

$\tfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$ (that is $30^\circ$ and $150^\circ$).

How long is the arc for $90^\circ$ on the unit circle? And on a wheel with a radius of 30 cm?

$\tfrac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57$. On the wheel: $30 \cdot \tfrac{\pi}{2} \approx 47.1$ cm.

In which intervals between $0$ and $2\pi$ does $y = \sin x$ increase, and where does it decrease? Give reasons using the unit circle.

Increasing from $0$ to $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ and from $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$ to $2\pi$, decreasing in between: the point rises on the right half of the circle.

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Amplitude, period and functions at a glance

The mains voltage in the home can be described by $U(t) = 325 \cdot \sin(100\pi \cdot t)$. The factor 325 gives the peak voltage in volts, the amplitude. The factor $100\pi$ determines how quickly everything repeats: the period is $\tfrac{2\pi}{100\pi} = 0.02$ s, so 50 oscillations per second.

KEY POINT · $y = a \cdot \sin(b \cdot x)$

Amplitude $|a|$: the values lie between $-|a|$ and $|a|$. If $a < 0$, the graph is reflected in the x-axis.

Period $p = \dfrac{2\pi}{b}$ (for $b > 0$): $b > 1$ compresses in the x-direction, $b < 1$ stretches.

230 volts? That is an average value of the alternating voltage (the RMS value), not the peak value.

INTERACTIVE · SINE WITH PARAMETERS

Change $a$ and $b$ and watch the amplitude and the period.

EXAMPLE 3 · READING OFF

A graph $y = a \sin(bx)$ varies between $-1.5$ and $1.5$ and has zeros at $0$, $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, … Find $a$ and $b$ ($a, b > 0$).

$a = 1.5$. Between two zeros there is half a period, so $p = \pi$ and $b = 2$.

EXAMPLE 4 · THE SWING

A swing swings with a largest displacement of 1.2 m, and one full oscillation takes 4 s. Set up an equation.

$a = 1.2$, $\tfrac{2\pi}{b} = 4$, so $b = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$: $s(t) = 1.2 \cdot \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} t\right)$.

INTERACTIVE · MEASURED CURVES

Real periodic processes: Ferris wheel, ebb and flow and more. Put the markers on two maximum points and read off the period.

EXERCISES

Give the amplitude and the period: a) $y = 3 \sin x$ b) $y = \sin(2x)$ c) $y = 0.5 \sin(0.5 x)$ d) $y = -2 \sin(4x)$.

a) 3; $2\pi$ b) 1; $\pi$ c) 0.5; $4\pi$ d) 2 (reflected); $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$

Calculate $y = 2 \sin x$ for $x = \tfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $y = \sin(2x)$ for $x = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$.

$2 \cdot 0.5 = 1$ and $\sin \tfrac{\pi}{2} = 1$.

In the harbour the water level varies between 1 m and 5 m; high tide is at 6:00 and again at 18:24. Give the mean value, the amplitude and the period.

Mean 3 m, amplitude 2 m, period 12 h 24 min.

Match them up: periodic, exponential, linear, quadratic? a) mobile phone tariff with a basic fee b) compound interest c) length of the day over the year d) braking distance

a) linear b) exponential c) periodic d) quadratic

A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 36 m, the axle is 20 m high, and one turn takes 10 min. The height of a gondola is $h(t) = 20 + 18 \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{5} t\right)$. Check the period and the highest and lowest points.

Period $\tfrac{2\pi}{\pi/5} = 10$ min. Highest point $20 + 18 = 38$ m, lowest $20 - 18 = 2$ m.

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Which values does $y = 4 \sin x$ take? What is the largest value of $y = 2 \sin(3x)$?

All values from $-4$ to $4$. Largest value 2.

Give the zeros of $y = \sin(2x)$ between $0$ and $\pi$.

$0$, $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$

A sine curve has the amplitude 3 and the period $\pi$. Give an equation.

$y = 3 \sin(2x)$

Connecting: compare the types of functions $y = 2x$, $y = x^2$, $y = 2^x$ and $y = \sin x$: which have a zero, which are periodic, which grow without limit?

Zeros: $2x$, $x^2$ (at 0) and $\sin x$ (infinitely many); $2^x$ none. Periodic: only $\sin x$. Growing without limit: $2x$, $x^2$, $2^x$.

OVERVIEW · TYPES OF FUNCTIONS

All the types of functions at a glance: graphs, domain, range and special features.

EXCURSIONNATURE

Why high tide comes later every day

On the North Sea there is high tide twice a day, but not always at the same time. The tides follow above all the moon, and it stands at the same place in the sky almost an hour later every day. That is why the period of the tides is about 12 hours and 25 minutes, not 12 hours.

The water level follows a sine curve quite well. Tide tables for harbours are still calculated today by superimposing many sine oscillations with different periods.

Source: Bundesamt für Seeschifffahrt und Hydrographie (BSH, Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency): Gezeitenvorausberechnung, Erläuterungen zu den Gezeitentafeln (tide prediction, notes on the tide tables).
